Synopsis:
A drow commander leading an attack on a group of tiefling refugees. She is following the orders of a new god, the Absolute, and is zealous and sadistic. In this situation, the player has sided with her and betrayed the tieflings - a fact she enjoys a great deal.

Cluster Contexts:
- DEN_AttackOnDen_Drow.json: Nightwarden Minthara is a True Soul drow commander leading a brutal raid on a den of tiefling refugees; she’s zealous for the Absolute, openly sadistic, and visibly pleased that the player has betrayed the fugitives to her. Off‑screen she has been interrogating and torturing prisoners (and may have a captured goblin) to learn the location of a nearby druid grove the Absolute wants reclaimed, and she punishes anyone not recognised as a True Soul. Because the player has sided with her, Minthara treats them as an ally and may expect them to help infiltrate or open the grove for the raiding party — important state flags (whether prisoners live, whether she knows the grove or its leader) were set by earlier Wolf Pens and camp confrontations. Nearby developments (grieving tieflings, goblin leaders, or Halsin’s rescue) and prior promises or companion involvement will shape NPC reactions and available dialogue.
- GOB_DrowAndCaptured_ThreeWayDialog.json: You and your party have been brought before Nightwarden Minthara in the goblin camp, escorted by a captured goblin (Sazza) you recovered from a nearby druid grove. Minthara wields authority and can probe minds; she learns the grove’s location from the goblin and intends to raid it, demanding the player’s cooperation — either by opening the gate and signalling the assault or by refusing and fighting her. The goblin’s fate hinges on whether she (or Minthara) recognises the player as a True Soul: if she does, Minthara will spare the prisoner; if not, Minthara will execute her unless you intervene. Off‑screen events in the camp (recent fights in the wolf pens, a druid/bear presence, and other encounters with goblin leadership) help explain the tension and the stakes but aren’t spelled out in these lines.
- GOB_DrowCommander.json: The player is standing in the goblin camp before Nightwarden Minthara, a drow True Soul who’s been sent to whip the goblins into shape and lead raids — she’s already had one success at the tavern and now wants the adventurers who infiltrated the camp found and reclaimed. Off‑screen the camp is tense from recent fights (the wolf pens combat and a freed/angry bear have unsettled the goblins) and a prisoner is being tortured for the location of a druid/tiefling sanctuary. Minthara can probe minds and forcibly mind‑meld the player to learn the grove’s whereabouts; she’s zealous, cruel, and quick to punish her subordinates (Rozzak) or extract promises from anyone she suspects is a True Soul. The player may have veiled or muddled memories—making Minthara suspicious—but if she believes the player is a True Soul she will order them to betray the grove or serve as her eyes for the coming hunt.
- DEN_AttackOnDen_RaidersArriveBeforeFight.json: Takes place immediately after the player blows the horn at the gates of the grove, beginning an attack on the refugees hiding there. The surviving tiefling leader rallies his troops, then the drow commander arrives with her retinue of goblins. She mind-melds with the player. She expects them - as True Souls - to betray the tieflings, and players must choose whether to side with her OR with the tieflings as the attack begins.

This is a huge fight and a decisive moment for the tieflings, the drow/goblins, AND the players.
- GOB_GoblinPriest_Branding.json: The sadistic goblin priestess is branding new converts to the cult of the Absolute. She is a True Soul - tadpoled, but unaware that is the case. She believes she is communing directly with the Absolute.

 She's one of three leaders in the goblin camp, and an important and powerful member of the Absolute's cult. She's cruel and has a sense of superiority over her own kind. Her offers of help are really a ploy to separate players from their friends so that she can imprison them and watch as the parasite eats them alive.

Dialogue Excerpts (up to 3 samples, ordered):
Sample 1:
- Nightwarden Minthara: I expect great things of you - when the battle begins, show me your worth. || [context] NodeContext: An aside to the player as she's gathering troops before setting out on a raid - (node 42)
- Player: I met True Soul Nere in the Underdark. He warned me against working with you. (node 66)
- Nightwarden Minthara: Did he, now? Let me guess: the snivelling brat's failed his duty. Nothing if not expected. (node 75)
- Nightwarden Minthara: But you - I can see you are different. Faithful to the last. (node 1)

Sample 2:
- Nightwarden Minthara: A glorious day. The Absolute will be pleased. (node 23)
- Nightwarden Minthara: But there is more to be done. This place is home to druids - root them out and kill them. (node 16)

Sample 3:
- Nightwarden Minthara: When you are done, we will celebrate our victory at your camp. (node 34)
- Player: Leave. (node 29)

context: Minthara is a True Soul drow commander leading a brutal Absolute raid on a den of tiefling refugees; off‑screen she has been interrogating and torturing prisoners (and may hold a captured goblin) to learn the location of a nearby druid grove the Absolute wants reclaimed. The player has already betrayed the tieflings and is being treated as an ally, so Minthara expects them to prove their worth — by opening the grove, signalling the assault, or otherwise aiding the raid. She can probe or mind‑meld minds to verify loyalty, is quick to punish perceived failures, and has been whipping the goblins into shape after recent camp fights. Earlier encounters (wolf pens, camp skirmishes, whether prisoners live or whether Minthara knows the grove/its leader) set state flags that determine what she knows and how she reacts.
